title: COMPLETENESS-CRITIC supplement — implicit-topology-or-jurisdiction-assumption specificity not covered by genericization-matrix.json
method: Reading-based transversal pass over the ng.aiday.policy source documents (main/, argumentation/, companion/, technical/, book/, book-public/), compared against every topology- and jurisdiction-related canonical matrix entry (ANCHOR-SINGLE-CAMPUS, ANCHOR-JURISDICTION, ANCHOR-CRPD-RATIFICATION, ANCHOR-AI-REGIME, ANCHOR-DATA-PROTECTION-REGIME, ANCHOR-TRANSFER-REGIME, ANCHOR-IDENTITY-FEDERATION, ANCHOR-NREN, ANCHOR-GEANT-BACKBONE, ANCHOR-EUROHPC-SYSTEM, ANCHOR-INSTITUTION-HPC, ANCHOR-ADMIN-LAW, ANCHOR-STATE-INFOSEC-POLICY, ANCHOR-ESSENTIAL-ENTITY-CLASSIFICATION) plus a full grep of genericization-matrix.json. The matrix is comprehensive for (a) single-campus geographic topology and (b) the pervasive EU/EEA legal vantage. The rows below are read-for-meaning implicit assumptions that the matrix does NOT isolate: the architecture structurally presumes that the adopting institution can and does SELF-HOST its core infrastructure and HOLD KEYS ON-PREMISES. book/ re-inputs already-covered main/companion/argumentation bodies and book-public/ is verbatim/extracted from main-body-EN.tex, so neither introduces new surface forms.

topologyAnchors.ANCHOR-SINGLE-CAMPUS: Single-campus / single-site GEOGRAPHIC topology (campus perimeter, campus network core, single data-centre, L2 VLAN fabric per zone). Covers physical campus geography, NOT the self-host/on-prem custody premise.
topologyAnchors.ANCHOR-NREN: National research-and-education-network connectivity and single-home-NREN framing.

jurisdictionAnchors.ANCHOR-JURISDICTION: Home jurisdiction Luxembourg/EU, '(including Luxembourg)' parentheticals, 'For institutions outside the EU ... transposes'.
jurisdictionAnchors.ANCHOR-CRPD-RATIFICATION: 'ratified by the EU and by Luxembourg'.
jurisdictionAnchors.ANCHOR-AI-REGIME / ANCHOR-DATA-PROTECTIO: Pervasive EU/EEA legal vantage (GDPR, NIS2, AI Act, Schrems II, third-country framing). The 'third-country' vantage point is already flagged as EU-bound.
jurisdictionAnchors.ANCHOR-ESSENTIAL-ENTITY-CLASSIFICATION: Public-administration-entity route / essential-entity-status-as-settled-fact (covers the public-institution status premise).
jurisdictionAnchors.ANCHOR-ADMIN-LAW / ANCHOR-STATE-INFOSEC-: National administrative-review law and national public-sector infosec baseline.

coveredByMatrixForReference.note: The two rows below are NOT instances of any of the above: ANCHOR-SINGLE-CAMPUS is about campus GEOGRAPHY (one site vs many), whereas these concern the orthogonal premise that the institution OWNS/OPERATES the infrastructure itself and physically holds trust anchors / keys on-premises — a capability and custody assumption that is invariant across single- and multi-site topologies and that a fully-cloud, small, or sovereign-cloud-mandated institution could not satisfy.

entries.genericDecision: Read-for-meaning: across the identity, compute, storage, crypto and workload chapters the reference instantiation presumes that the adopting institution self-hosts its core components (Keycloak, Ceph/enterprise storage, OpenStack/Kubernetes, Harbor, Vault/HSM) and operates them on infrastructure it controls. This is an implicit topology/capability assumption distinct from the single-campus geography already captured by ANCHOR-SINGLE-CAMPUS: it presumes the institution has the operational capacity, staffing and physical hosting footprint to run these services itself. A small institution, a deliberately cloud-native institution, or one in a jurisdiction that mandates a national/sovereign managed cloud could satisfy the same functional contract without self-hosting. Generalise the framing to 'the institution operates, or procures under equivalent custody guarantees, a deployment of ...' so that managed/sovereign-cloud and shared-NREN-operated realisations are first-class rather than implicitly second-class. The named products themselves are separately handled by ANCHOR-OSS-IMPL-EXAMPLES and the vendor anchors; this row is only about the self-host TOPOLOGY presumption.

entries.rationale: Self-hosted / institution-operated infrastructure as the default deployment topology. The architecture is genuinely standards-first and explicitly admits managed-CA and cloud-burst alternatives, but the spine of every layer's reference instantiation is a component the institution runs itself, and the alternatives still retain an on-premises custody core (e.g. ch13 keeps HYOK on 'the institutional Vault and HSM' even in the external-CA alternative). The matrix flags the campus GEOGRAPHY (ANCHOR-SINGLE-CAMPUS) and the OSS product names (ANCHOR-OSS-IMPL-EXAMPLES) but does not isolate the orthogonal premise that the institution is a self-hoster with its own operational footprint. Medium confidence: 'the institution operates X' is partly ordinary architecture-document phrasing, but as a cumulative pattern across five chapters it is a genuine, non-trivial scoping assumption a non-self-hosting adopter must re-read.

entries.title: On-premises key custody / no-third-country-disclosure as the structural data-sovereignty optimum
surfaceForms: On-premises storage, institutional key custody, no third-country disclosure regime. (sovereignty-grid 'Data: 3 Robust' driver)
the trust anchor [must be kept] under institutional custody regardless of [operational instantiation]
the trust anchor in an HSM under institutional custody
Trust anchor must be under institutional custody regardless of operational instantiation. This is structural, not optional. (coherence rule D13.6)
the institution operates [keys/anchor] under institutional custody; HYOK arrangements remain on the institutional Vault and HSM
entries.genericDecision: The sovereignty grid scores the data dimension 'Robust' precisely when storage is on-premises, keys are in institutional custody, and there is 'no third-country disclosure regime' — and the crypto chapter elevates on-premises trust-anchor custody to a 'structural, not optional' invariant. This bundles two implicit assumptions the matrix does not isolate together: (1) a TOPOLOGY assumption that the institution can physically hold its own HSM/Vault and trust anchor on premises (related to but distinct from TOPO-SELF-HOST-INSTITUTIONAL-CUSTODY: this row is about KEY/ANCHOR custody location specifically and its role as the scoring optimum); and (2) a JURISDICTION assumption that the institution's vantage is a jurisdiction in which on-premises custody is both achievable and the strongest available posture — the 'no third-country disclosure regime' criterion presupposes the EU/EEA 'third-country' framing (already EU-bound per ANCHOR-JURISDICTION/ANCHOR-TRANSFER-REGIME) AND a local legal order under which on-prem custody actually defeats disclosure (not true everywhere: a domestic compelled-access regime can reach an on-premises HSM, so 'on-prem = Robust' is itself jurisdiction-relative). Generalise so the data-dimension optimum is expressed as 'custody arrangement that minimises the applicable disclosure-regime exposure' rather than hard-coding on-premises custody, and gate the 'no third-country disclosure regime' criterion behind the adopter's jurisdiction profile.

entries.rationale: On-premises key custody / no-third-country-disclosure as the structural data-sovereignty optimum. The matrix flags the EU 'third-country' vantage (ANCHOR-JURISDICTION, ANCHOR-TRANSFER-REGIME) and the on-prem storage products, but does not flag that the grid's data-dimension SCORING treats on-premises institutional key custody as the invariant optimum — a posture that (a) presumes the institution can physically host an HSM/Vault, and (b) is jurisdiction-relative, since a domestic compelled-access or lawful-interception regime can reach an on-premises trust anchor, so 'on-prem custody = Robust' does not hold in every legal order. Medium confidence: the architecture defensibly argues for institutional custody as best practice within the EU vantage, but presenting it as a 'structural, not optional' scoring optimum embeds an implicit jurisdiction+topology premise that an agnostic template should parameterize.
